Interface RouteCondition

All Known Implementing Classes:
RouteCondition.AllOf, RouteCondition.AnyOf, RouteCondition.Cookie, RouteCondition.Custom, RouteCondition.Header, RouteCondition.Host, RouteCondition.Method, RouteCondition.Not, RouteCondition.PeerAddress, RouteCondition.Query, RouteCondition.RemoteAddress, RouteCondition.TimeWindow
public sealed interface RouteCondition permits RouteCondition.Header, RouteCondition.Query, RouteCondition.Cookie, RouteCondition.Method, RouteCondition.Host, RouteCondition.RemoteAddress, RouteCondition.PeerAddress, RouteCondition.TimeWindow, RouteCondition.AllOf, RouteCondition.AnyOf, RouteCondition.Not, RouteCondition.Custom
A declarative condition on a request, for RouteSpec.where(RouteCondition): on its headers, query parameters, cookies, method, host, client and peer addresses and the time it arrives, and their combinations. A condition is data: the router reads it, flattens and orders it cheapest first when the route is built, and shows it in the route info, which a lambda does not allow. custom(Predicate) takes a lambda for what the others do not express. 
import static io.micronaut.web.router.builder.RouteCondition.*;
import static io.micronaut.web.router.builder.ValueMatcher.*;

routes.GET("/search")
    .where(header("X-Beta").or(query("beta", equalTo("true"))))
    .order(-1)
    .handle(betaHandler);
routes.path("/admin", admin -> admin.where(peerAddress("10.0.0.0/8")));

A condition is data, not a predicate: only the router evaluates it, with the host and the client address as the server resolves them, see RouteCondition.Host and RouteCondition.RemoteAddress, and the clock of the application. Conditions combine with and(RouteCondition), or(RouteCondition) and negate(); a lambda is a custom(Predicate) condition.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    A request with a query parameter whose decoded value the matcher matches, one of its values if the parameter is repeated.

    RouteCondition.RemoteAddress
    A request from a client address in one of the ranges, as the server resolves it: with the client address resolver of the server, which reads the header that micronaut.server.client-address-header names, or else the forwarded headers of the request, or else the peer of the connection.
    static final record 
    RouteCondition.TimeWindow
    A request that arrives in a period, as the clock of the server tells: the Clock bean if there is one, otherwise the system clock.

    • remoteAddress

      static RouteCondition remoteAddress(String... cidrs)
      A request from a client address in one of the ranges, IPv4 or IPv6 in CIDR notation, e.g. remoteAddress("10.0.0.0/8", "192.168.1.7", "fd00::/8"): the address of the client as the server resolves it, see RouteCondition.RemoteAddress. An address without a prefix length is the range of that address alone. No name is ever looked up.

      The server resolves the address with its HttpClientAddressResolver, which trusts the X-Forwarded-For and Forwarded headers of the request unless micronaut.server.client-address-header is configured: a client can then send any address. Use it behind a trusted proxy that sets the configured header, and peerAddress(String...) for access control.

      Parameters:
      cidrs - The ranges of addresses, at least one
      Returns:
      The condition
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a range is not a range of addresses

    • peerAddress

      static RouteCondition peerAddress(String... cidrs)
      A request whose connection comes from an address in one of the ranges, IPv4 or IPv6 in CIDR notation, e.g. peerAddress("10.0.0.0/8", "::1"): the address of the peer of the connection, HttpRequest.getRemoteAddress(), never a forwarded address, so a client cannot spoof it with a header. This is the condition for access control, e.g. an allow or deny list. Behind a proxy the peer is the proxy: see remoteAddress(String...) for the address of the client the proxy forwards. A request without a peer address, or whose peer address is unresolved, does not meet the condition. No name is ever looked up.
      Parameters:
      cidrs - The ranges of addresses, at least one
      Returns:
      The condition
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a range is not a range of addresses
